Lido-Pellestrina (Venice Lido, Pellestrina) — Venice, Italy

Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

Genuine Italian press coverage (Il Gazzettino, La Nuova Venezia, VeneziaToday, La Voce di Venezia) from 2024-2026 shows Lido-Pellestrina remains a low-crime, mostly residential and resort area with no pattern of violent crime, muggings, or organized theft targeting tourists comparable to Venice's historic center. The main documented issue is opportunistic petty theft at Lido's beach establishments: a recurring pattern of bags, cash, credit cards, and keys stolen from beach umbrellas/cabins while owners swim (e.g. a Milan couple robbed of 500 euros and keys at a beach club in August 2025; a serial thief repeatedly targeting cabins at two well-known beaches), and occasional break-ins into parked cars near the vaporetto stops with thieves fleeing by boat. Venice Local Police ran a "Spiagge Sicure" enforcement operation on Lido beaches in July 2026, though it targeted illegal vendors, not violent crime. Drug-related arrests occur occasionally on Lido but at a level consistent with any Italian town, not a hotspot. A genuine, separate safety concern is traffic/pedestrian risk on Lido's main artery, Via Sandro Gallo, where at least two elderly pedestrians were struck and killed by vehicles in recent incidents (2024-2025) — a road-safety issue rather than crime. No evidence was found of nightlife violence, assault, harassment, or any notable crime pattern specific to Pellestrina, which press coverage confirms is a quiet fishing community; searches turned up only routine administrative/labor-safety checks there. Given the absence of violent crime or theft targeting people after dark, both day and night default to no particular concern, with the main practical caution being standard beach-bag vigilance and pedestrian care on the main road. Sources checked: La Nuova Venezia (nuovavenezia.it); Il Gazzettino (ilgazzettino.it); La Voce di Venezia (lavocedivenezia.it); La Piazza Web (lapiazzaweb.it); CityNext (citynext.it); VeneziaToday (veneziatoday.it); Il Nuovo Terraglio (ilnuovoterraglio.it).
